meaning.en: Kaikeyi repeatedly praises Manthara as wise and loyal, saying that the maid has become her support while she was being swept toward danger. She promises intimate favour if fate fulfils the plan. After honouring Manthara in many ways, Kaikeyi goes to the anger chamber and arranges the outward signs of injury and resentment. The poem compares Manthara's counsel to rain falling on the seed of disaster in Kaikeyi's distorted judgment: deceit makes it sprout into two boons whose fruit will be suffering. Outside, no one knows of the scheme; the palace and city remain busy with joyful preparations.
meaning.hi: कैकेयी मन्थरा को बार-बार बुद्धिमान और हितैषी कहती हैं और मानती हैं कि संकट में बहती हुई उन्हें उसी ने सहारा दिया है। योजना सफल होने पर वे उसे विशेष स्नेह और सम्मान देने का वादा करती हैं। मन्थरा का आदर करके कैकेयी कोपभवन में जाती हैं और रूठने तथा अपमानित होने के बाहरी चिह्न सजाती हैं। कविता मन्थरा की सलाह को विपत्ति के बीज पर बरसी वर्षा और कैकेयी की बिगड़ी बुद्धि को भूमि कहती है; कपट का जल पाकर वह बीज दो वरों के पत्तों और दुःख के फल में उगता है। बाहर किसी को इस चाल का पता नहीं और नगर उत्सव की तैयारी में लगा है।

title.en: Ayodhya celebrates while Dasharatha visits Kaikeyi
title.hi: अयोध्या उत्सव मनाती है और दशरथ कैकेयी के भवन जाते हैं

meaning.en: Ayodhya's people move in and out of Dasharatha's crowded court, preparing auspicious celebrations. Rama's childhood companions visit him in small groups; he recognizes their affection, welcomes them gently, and asks after their welfare. They leave praising his courtesy and wishing that, wherever future birth may take them, their bond of service and affection with Rama and Sita may endure. Against this citywide hope, Kaikeyi burns inwardly under the influence of the counsel she has accepted. At evening Dasharatha, unaware of the anger chamber and the hidden demands, goes happily to Kaikeyi's residence; the poem casts the approaching encounter as tenderness walking unknowingly toward cruelty.
meaning.hi: अयोध्या के स्त्री-पुरुष शुभ तैयारी करते हुए दशरथ के भीड़भरे दरबार में आते-जाते हैं। राम के बालसखा छोटे समूहों में उनसे मिलने आते हैं; राम उनके प्रेम को पहचानकर आदर देते हैं और कोमल वाणी में कुशल पूछते हैं। लौटते समय वे राम के स्वभाव और स्नेह की प्रशंसा करते हैं तथा कामना करते हैं कि किसी भी जन्म में राम-सीता के साथ उनका यह सेवक-स्वामी जैसा प्रेम बना रहे। पूरे नगर की इस आशा के विपरीत, स्वीकार की हुई सलाह के प्रभाव में कैकेयी भीतर ही भीतर जल रही हैं। संध्या को दशरथ कोपभवन और छिपी माँगों से अनजान होकर प्रसन्नतापूर्वक उनके भवन जाते हैं; कविता इसे स्नेह का कठोरता के निकट जाना कहती है।

बाल सखा सुनि हियँ हरषाहीं। मिलि दस पाँच राम पहिं जाहीं॥
प्रभु आदरहिं प्रेमु पहिचानी। पूँछहिं कुसल खेम मृदु बानी

फिरहिं भवन प्रिय आयसु पाई। करत परसपर राम बड़ाई॥
को रघुबीर सरिस संसारा। सीलु सनेहु निबाहनिहारा

जेहिं जेहिं जोनि करम बस भ्रमहीं। तहँ तहँ ईसु देउ यह हमहीं॥
सेवक हम स्वामी सियनाहू। होउ नात यह ओर निबाहू

अस अभिलाषु नगर सब काहू। कैकयसुता हृदयँ अति दाहू॥
को न कुसंगति पाइ नसाई। रहइ न नीच मतें चतुराई

साँझ समय सानंद नृपु गयउ कैकई गेहँ।
गवनु निठुरता निकट किय जनु धरि देह सनेहँ

title.en: Dasharatha finds Kaikeyi on the floor
title.hi: दशरथ कैकेयी को भूमि पर पड़े देखते हैं

meaning.en: Hearing that Kaikeyi is in the anger chamber, Dasharatha hesitates in fear. The poem contrasts a king before whom other rulers defer with a husband made helpless by desire and anxiety. He enters and finds Kaikeyi lying on the bare floor in old, coarse clothes, her ornaments thrown aside. The narrator reads the costume as a sign of threatened widowhood and imagines her anger as a serpent testing where to strike. Dasharatha does not yet know the demand. He approaches gently, touches her, repeatedly asks who has harmed her, and begs her to explain the cause of her anger. The danger lies in the staged scene and his lack of informed knowledge.
meaning.hi: कैकेयी के कोपभवन में होने का समाचार सुनकर दशरथ भय से ठिठक जाते हैं। कविता उस राजा का विरोधाभास दिखाती है जिसके संकेत पर दूसरे नरेश चलते हैं, पर जो कामना और चिंता में पत्नी के सामने असहाय हो गया है। भीतर वे कैकेयी को भूमि पर, पुराने मोटे वस्त्रों में और आभूषण उतारकर पड़े देखते हैं। कथावाचक इस वेश को आने वाले वैधव्य का संकेत और उनके क्रोध को वार की जगह खोजते सर्प की उपमा देता है। दशरथ अभी माँगों से अनजान हैं। वे कोमलता से पास जाकर स्पर्श करते हैं, बार-बार पूछते हैं कि किसने अनहित किया और क्रोध का कारण बताने की विनती करते हैं। संकट रचे हुए दृश्य और उनकी अनभिज्ञता में है।

कोपभवन सुनि सकुचेउ राऊ। भय बस अगहुड़ परइ न पाऊ॥
सुरपति बसइ बाहँबल जाकें। नरपति सकल रहहिं रुख ताकें

सो सुनि तिय रिस गयउ सुखाई। देखहु काम प्रताप बड़ाई॥
सूल कुलिस असि अँगवनिहारे। ते रतिनाथ सुमन सर मारे

सभय नरेसु प्रिया पहिं गयऊ। देखि दसा दुखु दारुन भयऊ॥
भूमि सयन पटु मोट पुराना। दिए डारि तन भूषन नाना

कुमतिहि कसि कुबेषता फाबी। अनअहिवातु सूच जनु भाबी॥
जाइ निकट नृपु कह मृदु बानी। प्रानप्रिया केहि हेतु रिसानी

केहि हेतु रानि रिसानि परसत पानि पतिहि नेवारई।
मानहुँ सरोष भुअंग भामिनि बिषम भाँति निहारई॥
दोउ बासना रसना दसन बर मरम ठाहरु देखई।
तुलसी नृपति भवतब्यता बस काम कौतुक लेखई॥

बार बार कह राउ सुमुखि सुलोचनि पिकबचनि।
कारन मोहि सुनाउ गजगामिनि निज कोप कर

title.en: Dasharatha swears by Rama and offers anything
title.hi: दशरथ राम की शपथ लेकर सब कुछ देने का वचन देते हैं

meaning.en: Trying to comfort Kaikeyi, Dasharatha offers the full reach of royal power: punishment for an enemy, wealth or rank for a poor person, even expulsion of another king. He says that his life, sons, household, subjects, and possessions are at her disposal. Most decisively, he swears by Rama that he is speaking truthfully and urges her to ask for whatever pleases her, dress again, and abandon the distressing disguise. Kaikeyi rises smiling after weighing the oath. The poem compares Dasharatha to a deer watching a hunter arrange the snare. His unlimited promise is made before he knows either request, so the oath is not informed consent to the specific exile that follows.
meaning.hi: कैकेयी को मनाने के लिए दशरथ राजसत्ता की पूरी पहुँच सामने रख देते हैं—किसी शत्रु को दंड, किसी निर्धन को धन या पद, यहाँ तक कि किसी राजा को देश से निकाल देना। वे कहते हैं कि उनके प्राण, पुत्र, परिवार, प्रजा और संपत्ति सब कैकेयी के वश में हैं। सबसे निर्णायक रूप से वे राम की शपथ लेकर अपने वचन को सत्य बताते हैं और कहते हैं कि जो मन चाहे माँग लें, फिर आभूषण पहनकर यह दुखद वेश छोड़ दें। शपथ का भार समझकर कैकेयी मुस्कराती हुई उठती हैं। कविता दशरथ की तुलना उस हिरन से करती है जो शिकारी को फंदा सजाते देख रहा हो। यह असीम वादा माँगें जाने बिना दिया गया है; आगे आने वाले वनवास के लिए यह सूचित सहमति नहीं है।

अनहित तोर प्रिया केइँ कीन्हा। केहि दुइ सिर केहि जमु चह लीन्हा॥
कहु केहि रंकहि करौं नरेसू। कहु केहि नृपहि निकासौं देसू

सकउँ तोर अरि अमरउ मारी। काह कीट बपुरे नर नारी॥
जानसि मोर सुभाउ बरोरू। मनु तव आनन चंद चकोरू

जौं कछु कहौं कपटु करि तोही। भामिनि राम सपथ सत मोही

बिहसि मागु मनभावति बाता। भूषन सजहि मनोहर गाता॥
घरी कुघरी समुझि जियँ देखू। बेगि प्रिया परिहरहि कुबेषू

यह सुनि मन गुनि सपथ बड़ि बिहसि उठी मतिमंद।
भूषन सजति बिलोकि मृगु मनहुँ किरातिनि फंद

title.en: The coronation news brings out the two old boons
title.hi: राज्याभिषेक का समाचार सुनकर दो पुराने वर सामने आते हैं

meaning.en: Still trusting Kaikeyi as a friend, Dasharatha joyfully announces that Rama will be installed as heir the next day and asks her to prepare for the celebration. The news strikes her painfully, but she hides the reaction behind a smile. The narrator criticizes the king for failing to see the deception and uses a broad period stereotype about women's conduct. Kaikeyi then reminds him that he repeatedly says 'ask' but has never delivered the two boons previously promised to her. By presenting the old debt as doubt about his generosity, she shifts the conversation from the unknown substance of her wishes to whether his word can be trusted. The actual demands are still withheld.

title.en: Dasharatha binds himself again to truth
title.hi: दशरथ स्वयं को फिर सत्य-वचन से बाँधते हैं

meaning.en: Dasharatha laughs off the complaint, saying that Kaikeyi never asked him to discharge the two stored promises and may ask for two or even four boons. He invokes the Raghu lineage's ideal that life may be lost but a pledged word must not be broken. He calls falsehood the greatest sin, names truth as the root of merit, cites received scriptural authority, and again seals the promise with an oath by Rama, whom he calls the limit of his virtue and affection. Kaikeyi now has the unconditional commitment she sought and prepares the frightening words that will destroy the king's joyful plan. The passage shows an oath being strategically elicited; it does not make coercive use of another's vow an ethical model.

title.en: Kaikeyi demands Bharata's crown and Rama's exile
title.hi: कैकेयी भरत का राज्य और राम का वनवास माँगती हैं

meaning.en: Kaikeyi finally names the two boons. First, Bharata must receive the royal consecration. Second, Rama must live as an ascetic exile in the forest for fourteen years. Her mild delivery makes the impact sharper. Dasharatha is stunned into silence, loses colour, covers his eyes, and holds his head as the coronation plan collapses. The poem imagines Kaikeyi uprooting his wish-fulfilling tree and devastating Ayodhya; the doha then voices a misogynistic period generalization about trusting a woman. Bharata has not been consulted, Rama has not consented, and the demand turns both sons into instruments of a promise made without knowledge of its terms.

meaning.en: Seeing Dasharatha silent, Kaikeyi challenges whether Bharata is truly his son and whether she was somehow bought rather than married into the household. She demands a direct answer: will he grant the boons or abandon his reputation for truth? She invokes Shibi, Dadhichi, and Bali as figures said to have surrendered body or wealth to keep a pledge, implying that a celebrated king must do likewise. Her words are described as salt rubbed into a burn. Dasharatha finally opens his eyes, strikes his head in anguish, and says the blow has landed at a fatal point. The cited exemplars belong to the poem's moral rhetoric; they do not prescribe self-harm, bodily sacrifice, or obedience to an unjust demand.

title.en: Dasharatha pleads that Rama and Bharata are his two eyes
title.hi: दशरथ कहते हैं कि राम और भरत उनकी दो आँखें हैं

meaning.en: Dasharatha sees Kaikeyi's anger as a drawn sword sharpened by cruel counsel and asks whether she intends to take his truth, his life, or both. Gathering himself, he pleads that Rama and Bharata are equally his two eyes. He promises to send for Bharata at dawn and, after choosing an auspicious day, install him publicly. He argues that Rama has no greed for kingship and loves Bharata deeply; his own error was only applying seniority in royal policy. meaning.en: Dasharatha swears that neither Kausalya nor anyone else prompted the coronation; he arranged it without consulting Kaikeyi, and now sees that omission as the cause of the ruined plan. title.en: Kaikeyi makes exile by dawn an ultimatum
title.hi: कैकेयी प्रभात तक वनवास की अंतिम शर्त रखती हैं

meaning.en: Dasharatha says that a fish might somehow live without water or a serpent without its jewel, but he cannot live without seeing Rama. His plea only intensifies Kaikeyi's anger. She dismisses every attempt to negotiate: either grant the promised boon or accept dishonour, she says, and she mocks praise of Rama, Dasharatha, and Kausalya. She frames her action as repayment for how Kausalya supposedly treated her. Her ultimatum is exact—if Rama does not leave in ascetic dress at dawn, her death and the king's disgrace will follow. The threat uses death and reputation to compel compliance; it must not be treated as free consent, healthy conflict, or a model for using self-harm language.

meaning.en: After delivering the ultimatum, Kaikeyi stands like a river of anger in flood. The poem extends the image: sin is the mountain, the two boons are hard banks, obstinacy the current, and Manthara's words the whirlpool; the flood tears at the tree of Dasharatha's kingship and runs toward an ocean of disaster. Realizing that the threat is firm, Dasharatha holds Kaikeyi's feet and begs her not to become the axe that fells his dynasty. He offers his own head but asks her to spare Rama by any means, warning that separation will burn within him for life. Unable to find a remedy, he falls to the ground striking his head and cries only 'Rama, Rama, Raghunath.'

title.en: Kaikeyi rejects retreat from the promise

meaning.en: Dasharatha lies physically slack, his throat dry and speech failing, like a fish out of water. Kaikeyi answers with still harsher words. If he was always going to retreat, why did he repeatedly invite her to ask? Can he be generous and miserly, truthful and evasive, at the same time? She tells him either to abandon the pledge openly or steady himself and fulfil it, adding a gendered taunt that he should not plead like a helpless woman. Hearing the attack, Dasharatha says the fault is not entirely hers and imagines destructive fate or a demon speaking through her. His collapse is literary distress, not a medical diagnosis; the gendered and supernatural explanations remain attributed, not endorsed.

title.en: Dasharatha predicts grief and Kaikeyi falls silent
title.hi: दशरथ पश्चात्ताप की चेतावनी देते हैं और कैकेयी मौन रहती हैं

meaning.en: Dasharatha insists that Bharata would never desire kingship and attributes Kaikeyi's judgment to hostile fate and his own past wrongdoing. He imagines Rama returning after exile to rule beautifully while all the brothers serve together and Rama's fame fills the three worlds. Yet, he says, Kaikeyi's stain and his regret will not disappear even after death. He asks her to hide her face from him and remain silent while he lives, warning that she will later repent like someone who kills a cow at the moment it comes seeking shelter. Exhausted, he falls again after countless pleas. Kaikeyi gives no answer and remains awake, compared by the narrator to a cremation ground; this silence records the scene, not her inner certainty.

title.en: A sleepless night ends in an ominous dawn
title.hi: निद्राहीन रात अशुभ प्रभात में बदलती है

meaning.en: Dasharatha spends the remaining night repeating Rama's name, like a bird disabled without wings. Inwardly he begs that dawn not come and that no one tell Rama. He even addresses the sun, asking it not to rise over the Raghu capital. The poem places the king's love for Rama and Kaikeyi's hardness at opposite limits set by fate. Dawn nevertheless arrives. Lutes, flutes, conches, heralds, and singers begin their customary auspicious sounds, but each reaches Dasharatha like an arrow. Festive ornaments are compared to adornment on a woman about to die with her husband—a harmful historical image, not a practice to romanticize. Outside, a sleepless city waits eagerly to see Rama and wonders why the king has not risen.
meaning.hi: दशरथ बची हुई रात राम-राम जपते हुए बिताते हैं, मानो पंख-विहीन पक्षी व्याकुल हो। मन में वे प्रार्थना करते हैं कि भोर न हो और कोई राम को समाचार न दे। वे सूर्य से भी कहते हैं कि रघुवंश की राजधानी पर न उगे। कविता राम के प्रति राजा के प्रेम और कैकेयी की कठोरता को विधाता द्वारा बनाई दो चरम सीमाएँ बताती है। फिर भी प्रभात होता है। वीणा, बाँसुरी, शंख, भाट और गायक अपने रोज़ के मंगल-स्वर आरंभ करते हैं, पर हर ध्वनि दशरथ को बाण जैसी लगती है। उत्सव के आभूषणों की तुलना पति के साथ मरने को सजाई स्त्री से की गई है—यह हानिकारक ऐतिहासिक छवि है, महिमामंडित करने योग्य प्रथा नहीं। बाहर निद्राहीन नगर राम-दर्शन की प्रतीक्षा में पूछता है कि राजा अभी तक क्यों नहीं जागे।

meaning.en: The ministers and attendants note that Dasharatha normally rises in the last watch and send Sumantra to wake him and receive instructions. Sumantra enters the royal apartments with growing dread; no one answers his questions, and he proceeds to Kaikeyi's room. After formally greeting the king he sees Dasharatha pale, overwhelmed, and collapsed on the floor like a lotus torn from its root. Fear keeps him from asking directly. Kaikeyi supplies a partial account: the king slept badly, spent the night repeating Rama's name, and will not disclose the reason. She then tells Sumantra to bring Rama quickly so that he may ask the news himself. Her control of information keeps both minister and son uninformed.

आनहु रामहि बेगि बोलाई। समाचार तब पूँछेहु आई॥
चलेउ सुमंत्रु राय रुख जानी। लखी कुचालि कीन्हि कछु रानी

सोच बिकल मग परइ न पाऊ। रामहि बोलि कहिहि का राऊ॥
उर धरि धीरजु गयउ दुआरें। पूँछहिं सकल देखि मनु मारें

समाधानु करि सो सबही का। गयउ जहाँ दिनकर कुल टीका॥
राम सुमंत्रहि आवत देखा। आदरु कीन्ह पिता सम लेखा

निरखि बदनु कहि भूप रजाई। रघुकुलदीपहि चलेउ लेवाई॥
रामु कुभाँति सचिव सँग जाहीं। देखि लोग जहँ तहँ बिलखाहीं

जाइ दीख रघुबंसमनि नरपति निपट कुसाजु॥
सहमि परेउ लखि सिंघिनिहि मनहुँ बृद्ध गजराजु
